The dive started in a habitat dominated by soft sediment with a few boulders. There were transitions between larger boulders to smaller boulders to soft sediment. We saw a queen snapper (​Etelis oculatus​) as soon as we arrived on the seafloor at a depth of 539 m. This is a new depth record for queen snapper, as they were only known to exist as deep as 450 m.
